title: Bacterial vaginosis: clue cells on wet mount
vignette: A 28-year-old woman comes to the office due to a vaginal discharge with an unpleasant odor. She describes a thin, grayish-white discharge with a fishy smell that is more noticeable after intercourse. She reports no vulvar itching, burning, or dysuria. Pelvic examination shows a homogeneous grayish-white discharge coating the vaginal walls, and the cervix appears normal without inflammation. Vaginal pH is 5.0 (normal 3.8-4.5). Which of the following findings is most likely seen on saline wet mount microscopy of the discharge?

clues.text: thin, grayish-white discharge with a fishy smell
clues.note: Thin grayish-white discharge with a fishy (amine) odor is the classic presentation of bacterial vaginosis from overgrowth of Gardnerella and anaerobes.

clues.text: no vulvar itching, burning, or dysuria
clues.note: Absence of itching/irritation argues against candidal vaginitis and against inflammatory trichomoniasis - bacterial vaginosis is typically non-inflammatory.
A non-inflamed cervix (no 'strawberry cervix') points away from Trichomonas and toward bacterial vaginosis.
Vaginal pH >4.5 (here 5.0 / normal 3.8-4.5) occurs in bacterial vaginosis as protective lactobacilli are replaced by anaerobes.

whatMatters: Thin grayish-white fishy discharge + vaginal pH >4.5 + non-inflamed cervix = bacterial vaginosis (Gardnerella vaginalis + anaerobe overgrowth replacing lactobacilli). Wet mount shows CLUE CELLS - vaginal EPITHELIAL CELLS COVERED WITH BACTERIA, giving a stippled border. Answer A.
strategy: Anchor on bacterial vaginosis (fishy odor, pH >4.5, positive whiff test, no inflammation). Its microscopic hallmark is the clue cell. Reject motile flagellates (Trichomonas), pseudohyphae/budding yeast (Candida), and abundant neutrophils (cervicitis/trichomoniasis) - bacterial vaginosis has few WBCs.

options.text: Epithelial cells covered with bacteria (clue cells)

eliminations.label: Motile flagellated organisms - Trichomonas
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: motile flagellated protozoa on wet mount = Trichomonas vaginalis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: trichomoniasis causes a frothy yellow-green discharge with itching and a strawberry cervix, not a thin non-inflammatory grayish discharge. ✅ Correct if: frothy discharge + strawberry cervix + motile flagellates.

eliminations.label: Pseudohyphae and budding yeast - Candida
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: pseudohyphae/budding yeast on KOH = candidal vaginitis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: candidiasis causes a thick white 'cottage cheese' discharge with intense itching and normal pH (<4.5), not a fishy discharge with pH 5.0. ✅ Correct if: thick white discharge + itching + normal pH.

eliminations.label: Gram-positive cocci in chains - not a vaginitis pattern
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: streptococci (gram-positive cocci in chains). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this is not the finding in bacterial vaginosis; BV shows epithelial cells coated with pleomorphic bacteria (clue cells). ✅ Correct if: describing a streptococcal culture, not a BV wet mount.

eliminations.label: Neutrophils with intracellular diplococci - gonococcal cervicitis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: many neutrophils with gram-negative intracellular diplococci = gonorrhea. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: bacterial vaginosis is non-inflammatory (few WBCs) and the cervix here is normal. ✅ Correct if: purulent cervicitis with intracellular diplococci.

reasoning: Thin grayish-white fishy discharge + pH 5.0 + non-inflamed cervix = bacterial vaginosis
BV = Gardnerella + anaerobe overgrowth replacing lactobacilli
Microscopic hallmark = clue cells (epithelial cells studded with adherent bacteria)
-> epithelial cells covered with bacteria; answer A
mechanism: Bacterial vaginosis results from loss of protective, hydrogen-peroxide-producing lactobacilli and overgrowth of Gardnerella vaginalis and anaerobes (e.g., Prevotella, Mobiluncus). Anaerobic metabolism raises vaginal pH above 4.5 and generates volatile amines (putrescine, cadaverine); alkalinization with 10% potassium hydroxide volatilizes these amines to produce the fishy odor (positive 'whiff' test). The diagnostic microscopic finding is the CLUE CELL: a squamous vaginal epithelial cell so densely coated with adherent coccobacilli that its cell border becomes stippled and indistinct. Notably, bacterial vaginosis is non-inflammatory, so few neutrophils are present - distinguishing it from trichomoniasis and cervicitis. Amsel criteria (≥3 of 4): thin homogeneous discharge, pH >4.5, positive whiff test, and clue cells. Treatment is metronidazole or clindamycin.

difficulty.label: 📚 Pure knowledge gap
difficulty.message: First Aid Micro/Repro > bacterial vaginosis: Gardnerella + anaerobes, clue cells, pH >4.5, positive whiff test (Amsel criteria), non-inflammatory, treat with metronidazole.

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: Recognize BV from the discharge/pH/non-inflamed cervix, then recall its wet-mount signature (clue cells).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on clue cell, whiff test, Gardnerella, lactobacilli, or Amsel criteria? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: Motile flagellates = Trichomonas; pseudohyphae = Candida; abundant neutrophils/intracellular diplococci = gonococcal cervicitis - all inflammatory, unlike BV.

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: BV -> clue cells, pH >4.5, whiff test positive, few WBCs; treat metronidazole.

keywords.front: Epithelial cell coated with bacteria (stippled border)

keywords.back: KOH releases amines -> fishy odor (bacterial vaginosis)
